assessment.nobel_worthiness: Changed how economists and policymakers understand technology, trade and labour demand. The task-based framework, the race between education and technology, and the local labour market effects of import competition all shaped research and public debate. The work combines credible empirical design with conceptual framing, and its policy relevance is high.
assessment.attribution: Katz and Autor are central to the skill-demand and wage-inequality literature, and Autor is also central to the task approach. Autor, Dorn and Hanson are the core of the China-shock work. Hanson is the strongest third name for the trade-shock strand. Dorn is a close alternative but more junior, and Acemoglu's overlapping contributions were already recognised. Three names cannot cover every strand, which leaves some attribution tension.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The core papers date from the 1990s to 2013 and have had more than a decade of replication, extension and debate, including on the persistence and interpretation of the China shock.
uncertainties: Recent labour-economics prizes may reduce the room for a further labour prize.
The China-shock interpretation is still debated, including its magnitude and its link to technology.
The three-name limit forces a choice between the technology strand and the trade strand.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting reshaped international trade theory and empirics. It introduced new channels for gains from trade, the reallocation of resources across firms, and a link between micro-level data and aggregate outcomes. It is arguably the most important trade advance since the new trade theory recognised in 2008.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the foundational model. Helpman, with Melitz and Yeaple, extended it to firm-level export and FDI choices and also contributed earlier to monopolistic-competition trade theory. Redding has important quantitative and spatial extensions but is a more distant contributor to the core idea. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are not on the list but are relevant to the empirical foundations.
assessment.maturity: Mature. More than two decades of impact on theory, data work and policy analysis.
uncertainties: Credit for firm-level trade facts could extend to scholars outside the credited set.
Quantitative-trade work in B006 overlaps conceptually, so the committee might prefer a different combination.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Created the law-and-finance research programme, which showed that investor protection, legal origin and ownership structure matter for financial development and corporate governance. It is widely cited, influenced policy and opened new empirical areas in corporate finance and comparative institutions.
assessment.attribution: The core papers, 'Law and Finance' and 'Legal Determinants of External Finance', are by La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny. Shleifer, La Porta and Lopez-de-Silanes are the most consistent contributors across the research programme. Vishny's contribution to the corporate-finance and behavioural-finance strands is substantial and creates a credit problem at three names.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with 25 or more years of scholarship. Its causal claims are contested.
uncertainties: Legal-origin identification has been challenged on causal interpretation, measurement and reliability of the indices.
The 2024 prize on institutions and prosperity may affect how the committee views the topic.
Shleifer's broader contributions across several fields could be weighed, and the three-name limit excludes Vishny.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reframed cross-country income differences as partly due to the misallocation of resources across firms, linking micro-level productivity dispersion to aggregate TFP. It has been influential in growth, development and industrial policy, and it improved the measurement of distortions in China and India.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) is the key paper. Restuccia and Rogerson (2008) is the other foundational paper, and Rogerson is not on the credited list. Restuccia has important agricultural-productivity work, so a two-name selection leaves attribution uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature. About 15 to 17 years of impact. The framework is still being refined and has been tested in many settings.
uncertainties: Results depend on model assumptions and data measurement, including how adjustment costs and markups are treated.
The credit split with Restuccia and Rogerson is difficult.
Possible overlap with recent growth-related prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: 'Credit Cycles' established how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks, a core mechanism in macro-finance models. It is a foundational framework for the analysis of financial crises, leverage and asset prices.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are clearly identified with this contribution. Gertler and Gilchrist are linked to the financial-accelerator empirical and quantitative strand, building on Bernanke, Gertler and Gilchrist, and Bernanke was already recognised in 2022.
assessment.maturity: Mature. Nearly 30 years of use, and the post-2008 literature confirmed its relevance.
uncertainties: The relationship between the collateral-constraint approach and the financial-accelerator approach raises attribution questions.
Empirical validation of specific mechanisms is more mixed than the theory's influence suggests.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Developed the empirical and sufficient-statistics approach to optimal taxation, centred on the elasticity of taxable income. It connects public-finance theory with administrative data and has had a large influence on tax design debates and research practice.
assessment.attribution: Slemrod's work on taxable-income responses and tax avoidance predates much of the sufficient-statistics literature, and Saez's work on bunching, top-income taxation and optimal tax formulas is central. Chetty and Stantcheva are important but more recent, and their credit is more tied to the next generation of the field. Feldstein's earlier ETI work is not on the list.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature for Saez and Slemrod. The early ETI work is 25 or more years old, but the sufficient-statistics agenda is still evolving.
uncertainties: Saez also appears in B010 on inequality, so there could be a conflict over credit.
Estimated elasticities depend on context and identification.
Chetty and Stantcheva may be preferred by a committee that favours younger candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Arellano-Bond and Arellano-Bover/Blundell-Bond estimators became standard tools in applied microeconomics and macroeconomics for dynamic panel models. Their practical impact in applied work is very large and spans many fields.
assessment.attribution: The credited trio plausibly captures the central GMM dynamic panel methods. Anderson-Hsiao, Hansen and Holtz-Eakin, Newey and Rosen are not on the list but are part of the intellectual lineage, which makes attribution difficult.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The estimators have been in use for 30 or more years.
uncertainties: Weak-instrument and proliferation problems in applied use may reduce perceived robustness.
Methodological prizes depend on how the committee weighs applied utility against conceptual novelty.
Blundell's wider contributions might be considered separately.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Developed the modern formal and empirical framework for political economics, covering electoral rules, constitutions, state capacity and fiscal outcomes. It links political institutions to economic policy and development, with real policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are strongly associated with comparative constitutional and electoral-rule analysis, and Besley with state capacity and accountability. Persson is Swedish and a former Committee member, so a conflict of interest would be disclosed. Acemoglu, Robinson and others, including the recent institutions laureates, also contributed to the field.
assessment.maturity: Mature. Roughly 25 to 30 years of influence, and the work is still widely taught and extended.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 institutions prize may reduce marginal room.
Identification of institutional effects, such as electoral rules and constitutions, is often hard.
Disclosed conflict of interest because of Swedish ties, not adjudicated here.
